title: Ang 684–685: the ninth Guru in Dhanasri
hookLine: why search the forest, on ang 684
tomorrow: why would a hymn in scripture ask for lentils and ghee?

lines: A SHIP IN A STORM, A PROMISE.
cards: The cabin listing promises no wifi, no neighbors, only pines: come find yourself. Here's an older version of that trip. Tradition tells of Makhan Shah, a trader whose ship nearly went down in a storm.
He promised the Guru an offering of gold if he lived. He lived. Now he's standing in the village of Bakala, and the houses are full of men, each one saying, I'm the Guru.

teach.h: HOUSE TO HOUSE, A SMALL OFFERING.
teach.b: Tradition says he went from claimant to claimant, leaving a small offering with each. Each one took it and blessed him.
Then, in a quiet room, he found a man deep in meditation, who looked up and asked about the rest of what he'd promised.
Makhan Shah ran to the roof and shouted: guru ladho re, I've found the Guru. That quiet man was Guru Tegh Bahadur, the ninth Guru.
And on ang 684, in Dhanasri, he turns the search around. In paraphrase: why go looking for him in the forest? He lives in everything, untouched, and he's with you too.
As fragrance lives inside the flower, as a reflection lives inside the mirror, so the Lord lives within, without a break. Search inside, brothers.
Know the One within and the One outside; that's the Guru's wisdom. And the last line: without knowing yourself, the moss of doubt won't clear. So the story and the hymn point the same way.

The trader crossed water and went house to house, and the answer was the one who already knew what was in his heart. The hymn doesn't sneer at the forest. It just says you can't leave the fragrance behind when you go.

how: Guru Tegh Bahadur's hymns, including 'why search the forest' on ang 684, are sung in kirtan in gurdwaras, and Sikhs tell the story of Makhan Shah finding him at Bakala.

s: Guru Tegh Bahadur tells seekers to go to the forest to find God
he asks why you'd search the forest, when the One lives within, like fragrance in a flower.
the hymn uses a reflection in a mirror as a picture of the One within
as fragrance in the flower, as a reflection in the mirror, so the Lord lives within.
tradition says Makhan Shah picked the claimant who blessed him most warmly
tradition says he found a quiet man who asked about the rest of what he'd promised.

games.q: your friend has a hard choice coming and says she can't think at home. she's booked a trip far away to 'find herself.' what fits ang 684?
o: go; God is only really found in quiet places far from home.
the trip can help, but what she's looking for travels with her.
don't go; leaving home to search shows a lack of faith.
games.why: the hymn doesn't forbid the forest. it asks why you'd search there, when the One lives within, like fragrance in a flower, and it goes where you go.

practice: Find something near you with a scent: tea, soap, a flower, the sleeve of a sweater. Breathe it in once, slowly, then keep it close for the sit and let the breath settle.
The scent isn't somewhere else; it's in the thing, the way the hymn says the One is in you.

wordCard.voice: Ang 684. Where the ninth Guru asks why you'd search the forest, when the One lives within, like fragrance in a flower.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: khoj, search; the hymn asks why you'd go searching (khojan) in the forest (ang 684).

carryVoice: Within: the fragrance goes wherever the flower goes, and so does what you went looking for. Day fifteen twenty-seven, found.
